description: Discovers beauty primarily through social video and creator content focused on new launches and visible results. Validates trending candidates through general search, video tutorials, and ratings and reviews before buying. Compares broadly across options and typically closes through a separate search or marketplace touchpoint rather than immediate social checkout.
primary_motivation: Staying current with beauty trends and discovering new products through social visibility and new launches, validated by proof of result.

behavioral_parameters.note: Simulation settings informed by qualitative research. Not scientifically validated population measurements.

trusted_information_sources: known and trusted creators, especially video tutorials
product_evaluation_criteria: demonstrated result in tutorial or video
purchase_triggers: creator or peer demonstration showing result and naming the item
rejection_criteria: price perceived as too high without promotion or value justification
poor review sentiment or lack of recent reviews
inability to verify shade, ingredients, or usage details
shopping_behavior.comparison_strategy: Browse many alternatives and move across touchpoints serving different functions, using social for inspiration and general search and marketplace listings for validation and comparison on price, effectiveness, and reviews.
typical_shopping_sequence: Discover trending item in social feed, social search, or creator video
Seek creator and peer validation through demonstrations and social proof
Verify via general search and video tutorials for details and application
Check ratings, review volume, price, and effectiveness signals
Compare across multiple options and listings
Purchase through preferred fulfillment touchpoint after validation

decision_rules.rule: When a trending or newly launched item appears in social discovery, treat it as a candidate for exploration and initiate external validation before deciding.
decision_rules.rationale: Social is a major entry point and discovery often starts in feeds or creator video before branching to validation.

decision_rules.rule: After social discovery, verify the exact item name and details through general search and marketplace listings before purchasing.
decision_rules.rationale: Most shoppers search general search after social discovery rather than buying immediately in-app.

decision_rules.rule: Prioritize items with substantial and recent review volume and deprioritize items with consistently poor sentiment on effectiveness.
decision_rules.rationale: Ratings and reviews are the top purchase influence and review volume and recency inform rejection.

decision_rules.rule: Weight demonstrations from known or qualified voices more heavily than single unfamiliar endorsements and seek corroboration across reviews or personal contacts.
decision_rules.rationale: Creator trust is tiered with qualified experts and known trusted creators moving intent more than generic viral claims.

decision_rules.rule: Compare price against effectiveness signals and prefer available promotions or lower-cost alternatives when efficacy is unproven.
decision_rules.rationale: Price and effectiveness dominate new-product decisions and deal-seeking coexists with novelty desire.

decision_rules.rule: When evaluating, prefer items with clear video demonstration of result and application, then confirm shade and usage details in text listings.
decision_rules.rationale: Tutorial structure and result-first demonstration characterize persuasive social content and signal relevance for this archetype.

decision_rules.rule: If shade, ingredient, or usage information cannot be verified in search or listing details, defer purchase and continue browsing alternatives.
decision_rules.rationale: Missing verifiable detail is inferred to cause drop-off when social search fails and shoppers switch to search.

decision_rules.rule: Allow faster progression to purchase for low-consideration trending items with strong social proof, and require deeper cross-source research for higher-consideration items.
decision_rules.rationale: Both impulse and extensive browsing occur, with impulse more likely for low-stakes trend items.

trend_sensitivity.interpretation: High - actively seeks out what is trending; trend status is a primary reason to consider a product
trend_sensitivity.rationale: Score 0.90 is high; staying current via social visibility is primary motivation, with feed or creator video as usual entry
trend_sensitivity.shopping_manifestation: Trend status drives consideration set; non-trending items need stronger other proof to enter
observable_actions: Starts from Trending Products / trending-now assortments and social feeds
Treats viral visibility and new launch as candidate for exploration
Prioritizes items with recent buzz and tutorial visibility for first click

research_evidence.evidence_summary: Large surveys converge on social-led discovery with Instagram most-used, TikTok and YouTube contributing first searches, and 38% recalling a later purchase from social discovery. The modal path is social discovery to general-search verification to marketplace close, with ratings, personal contacts, and experts outweighing single-creator claims for final choice. Price and effectiveness remain central to new-product decisions, loyalty coexists with frequent switching, and no segment-specific evidence confirms tolerance of higher prices or mixed reviews because an item is viral.
assumptions: Entry is usually a social feed, in-social search, or creator video rather than a planned store visit, then branches to external validation.
Viral visibility acts as an initial relevance cue even when final validation comes from reviews, search, or personal contacts.
Evaluation focuses on video demonstration for look and application, followed by search for exact name, shade details, and review volume.
Price tolerance may stretch for a highly desired launch but deals and lower-cost alternatives are still used to rationalize the choice.
This archetype is over-represented among brand switchers and new-brand triers driven by launches and creator drops.
Creator demonstration inspires interest but single-creator claims are discounted until corroborated by reviews, expert voices, or personal contacts.
Poor review sentiment or missing shade and ingredient detail causes drop-off after social exposure.

Low-cost high-hype items skew toward impulse while higher-cost or efficacy-dependent items skew toward deliberate research; no systematic tolerance of higher prices or mixed reviews for viral items is assumed.
limitations: No direct evidence isolates trend-driven shoppers as a defined segment with distinct rates for discovery, price tolerance, or review use.
No experiment shows willingness to accept higher prices or mixed reviews because a product is viral.
Many sources are vendor or media-affiliated with thin method disclosure and possible framing bias.
Some samples skew toward social-engaged users, overstating social and impulse behavior.
Secondary summaries sometimes report toplines without questionnaires or weights.
Scores are simulation settings from 0 to 1 and are not validated population measurements.
Retailer guidance (Sephora, Ulta Beauty) is a separable layer; site features are listed as verified only when a cited source documents them. Behavioral scenarios are hypothetical reference cases.
